title: Analyzing the Protein Terminome of Human Cancer Cell Line Culture Supernatants
author: Tsumagari, Chang, et al.

steps.title: Seed A431 cells
steps.instruction: Seed 5–10 × 10⁶ A431 cells onto each of eighteen 15 cm dishes (3 dishes × 3 replicates × 2 conditions) the day before conditioning; aim for ~90 % confluence at the start of conditioning.

steps.title: Wash cells with PBS(+)
steps.instruction: Wash the cells three times with 20 mL of PBS(+) per dish to remove serum.

steps.title: Inhibitor pretreatment
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL fresh serum‑free medium containing 10 µM BB‑94 (or DMSO as control) to each dish and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified for 1 h.

steps.title: Activate shedding with PMA
steps.instruction: Remove the pretreatment medium, add 10 mL fresh serum‑free medium containing 1 µM PMA and 10 µM BB‑94 (or DMSO) to each dish and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 1 h.

steps.title: Collect and pool supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the culture supernatant on ice; pool the supernatants from three dishes (total 30 mL) to form one biological replicate.

steps.title: Clarify supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the pooled conditioned medium at 3,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C; transfer the cleared supernatant to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Add protease inhibitors
steps.instruction: To the 30 mL cleared medium add 0.3 mL 200 mM EDTA‑NaOH, 0.3 mL 200 mM EGTA‑NaOH, 0.3 mL 100 mM PMSF, and 30 µL 100× protease‑inhibitor cocktail (final 0.1 %); mix gently.

steps.title: Concentrate sample
steps.instruction: Transfer the inhibited medium to an Amicon Ultra centrifugal filter and centrifuge at 3,000 × g, 4 °C until the volume is reduced to ~200 µL (typically 4–7 h).

steps.title: Methanol‑chloroform precipitation
steps.instruction: To the 200 µL concentrate add 600 µL methanol (3 × vol), vortex 1 min; add 150 µL chloroform (0.75 × vol), vortex 1 min; add 450 µL ultrapure water (2.25 × vol), vortex 1 min; centrifuge 20,000 × g for 5 min at 25 °C; discard the upper aqueous phase; add 450 µL methanol (2.25 × vol) and gently mix by swinging (no vortex); centrifuge 20,000 × g for 5 min at 25 °C; remove supernatant and dry the protein pellet by leaving the tube open for 2 min.

steps.title: Dissolve protein pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 200 µL PTS buffer (sonication if needed) and measure protein concentration using a BCA assay (alternatives: Bradford).

steps.title: Reduce and alkylate proteins
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of 100 mM TCEP (1/10 vol) and 20 µL of 400 mM CAA (1/10 vol) to the protein solution, vortex, and incubate at 95 °C for 5 min; recalculate protein concentration accounting for the added volumes.

steps.title: Peptide purification with StageTips
steps.instruction: Dissolve the peptide sample in 20–40 µL buffer A (add 2 M guanidine‑HCl or sonicate 2–5 min if needed). Prepare SDB‑XC StageTips in 2 mL microtubes. Condition each tip with 50 µL buffer B. Equilibrate with 50 µL buffer A (stop before buffer fully exits). Load the peptide solution and pass through. Wash with 50 µL buffer A. (For C2, total 60 µg peptide = 10 µg × 6 samples; split into three equal parts and use three StageTips.) Store loaded tips at –20 °C if needed. Elute peptides with 50 µL buffer B, collect eluate, and dry in a SpeedVac.

steps.title: Data analysis and statistics
steps.instruction: Import MaxQuant “Peptides.txt”, exclude peptides with missed cleavages, and separate N‑terminal (LysargiNase) and C‑terminal (trypsin/LysC) peptides based on enzyme‑specific termini. Extract proteolytic peptides whose termini do not match the respective enzyme specificity. Perform median normalization of log₂‑converted TMT intensities per channel. Define membrane proteins using UniProt keywords “GPI‑anchor” and “transmembrane”. Use Perseus to generate volcano plots with default parameters (randomization = 250, FDR < 0.05, S0 = 0.1).

description: Analyzing protein termini on a proteome scale, called terminomics, is a powerful approach to characterize the proteoform through defining both the N- and C-termini. Protein shedding can be transiently upregulated by certain agonists, such as phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), via activation of metalloproteases which have emerged as the major sheddase family (Huovila et al., 2005). To achieve large-scale identification of ectodomain shedding sites cleaved by members of the metalloprotease family, a quantitative terminomics workflow consisting of shedding activation with PMA, broad-spectrum metalloprotease inhibitor (BB-94; batimastat) treatment, SCX-based terminal peptide enrichment, TMT labeling and nano-scale liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (nanoLC/MS/MS) measurement is employed. This protocol is applicable to any cultured cells that can be maintained in serum-free medium during medium conditioning, and we have applied it to a panel of ten human cancer cell lines (Tsumagari et al., 2021). We have also used this protocol for lysates and culture supernatants of other human cell lines such as HEK293T. The protocol below describes the specific steps for the culture supernatant of A431 cells, a human cell line derived from epidermoid carcinoma, selected as a typical adherent mammalian cell line. Follow the workflow shown in Figure 1 for sample preparation. In the workflow of N-terminomics (left side of Figure 1), N-terminal peptides are enriched followed by TMT labeling, while in the workflow of C-terminomics (right side of Figure 1), C-terminal peptides are enriched after TMT-labeling. This difference is due to the difference of charge distribution between LysargiNase digests (used for N-terminal peptide enrichment) and trypsin/LysC digests (used for C-terminal peptide enrichment), which affects the terminal peptide enrichment efficiency of SCX.Figure 1Schematic workflowConditioned media from three 15 cm dishes are pooled to make a replicate.
